record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.context_brief: Massless axially symmetric solutions and geons
record.original_question: Do compactly supported stationary axially symmetric solutions of the massless Einstein-Vlasov system exist, with the density function vanishing outside a compact set so that the interior massless Vlasov solution could be glued to a vacuum exterior, and what would such solutions imply for Wheeler-type geons modeled by photon-gas matter?

evidence.quote: A question related to the opening of this review and to the existence of compact solutions is whether or not massless axially symmetric solutions exist.

Hence, the crucial question is whether or not massless axially symmetric solutions can be constructed such that the density function vanishes outside a compact set. If so, it would be possible to glue the solution to a vacuum solution –although no explicit vacuum solution exists as in the spherically symmetric case.
Hence, the question whether or not axially symmetric solutions of the massless Einstein-Vlasov system exist is closely related to the existence of Wheeler’s original conception of geons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system for a collisionless gas of massless particles on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime (M,g). Let f ≥ 0 be a distribution function on the mass-shell bundle P₀ = {(x,p) ∈ TM : g_x(p,p) = 0, p future-directed}, which is conserved along the geodesic flow:

   p^α ∂_{x^α} f − Γ^α_{βγ} p^β p^γ ∂_{p^α} f = 0.

The energy-momentum tensor is

   T_{αβ}(x) = ∫_{P₀,x} f(x,p) p_α p_β μ_x(p),

with μ_x the natural volume form on the null cone at x, and (g, f) satisfy the Einstein equations R_{αβ} − (1/2) R g_{αβ} = 8π T_{αβ}.

Assume the spacetime is stationary and axially symmetric, i.e. admits two commuting Killing vector fields ∂_t (timelike at infinity) and ∂_φ (with closed orbits), and assume asymptotic flatness. Let ρ(x) denote the matter density, e.g. ρ(x) = T_{αβ}(x) n^α n^β for a chosen timelike observer n.

Questions:

(a) Do there exist nontrivial stationary, axially symmetric, asymptotically flat solutions (g, f) of the massless Einstein–Vlasov system for which the support of f projects to a compact set K ⊂ M, so that ρ ≡ 0 outside K?

(b) If such solutions exist, can the interior solution be matched (glued) across ∂K to an exterior vacuum solution of the Einstein equations (with appropriate junction conditions), thereby yielding a globally regular asymptotically flat spacetime?

(c) Equivalently, do there exist Wheeler-type geons modeled by a photon-gas (massless Vlasov) matter source, i.e. self-gravitating, long-lived, compactly supported configurations of null particles in axial symmetry?

Prove or disprove the existence of such solutions, and characterize their geometric and matter-theoretic properties.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate this question is identified as an open problem in the mathematical relativity literature on stationary axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov solutions. Existence results exist for the massive axisymmetric case and for the massless case around a Schwarzschild black hole, but no construction of compactly supported stationary axisymmetric massless solutions (photon-gas geons) appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Axially Symmetric Static Solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov System
status_evidence.snippet: Existence proof for axisymmetric static solutions, in the massive case.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is established for massive axially symmetric static Einstein–Vlasov solutions, leaving the massless analogue open.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Steady States of the Massless Einstein–Vlasov System Surrounding a Schwarzschild Black Hole
status_evidence.snippet: Steady-state massless Einstein–Vlasov solutions constructed around a Schwarzschild black hole.
status_evidence.claim: Massless steady states are constructed only in spherical symmetry around a black hole, not as compactly supported axisymmetric geons.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Review listing the existence of compactly supported stationary massless axisymmetric solutions and their relation to Wheeler's geons as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: This question is explicitly listed as an open problem.
